text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer is given training data—examples that include both input and the correct answer. Using this data, the system builds a model, which is essentially a mathematical pattern that connects inputs to outputs. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For example, it might predict whether an email is spam or not. The quality of the model is measured by its accuracy, meaning how often its predictions match the real results. The better the training data, the more accurate the model becomes.
